note: Both sets cover essentially the same steel section callouts (W8X10, W10X12, W6X20, HSS4X4X1/4, HSS4X6X1/4, L3x3x1/4, L4X4X5/16, PL3X1/4, C8X11.5) with largely identical, page-supported quotes and elevation conditions. Set A adds one claim with an invented condition ('vertical member') not present anywhere on the page, plus a detail-reference condition (S-301 A4) that is at best loosely bound. Set B avoids invented content but repeats the same facts more times (L3x3x1/4 and HSS4X4X1/4 each appear several times under slightly different attribute names). Both sets omit the key elevation datums (T.O. STEEL 11'-4", FIRST FLR 2'-4", SOLAR ENVELOPE 18'-0", GRADE LEVEL 0" is only partly captured) and the overall dimensions, and both use vague entities such as 'component'/'framing member' and the odd 'W10X | weight' claim.
remarks: Text layer is a flattened concatenation of four elevation callout blocks, so member-to-elevation binding cannot be verified precisely from text alone; both sets' elevation conditions are broadly consistent with the block ordering but not provable. Both sets miss the elevation datums (T.O. STEEL 11'-4", FIRST FLR 2'-4", SOLAR ENVELOPE 18'-0") and overall dimensions (32'-0", 27'-8", 8'-8 5/8", 8'-8 1/2"). The claim 'W10X | weight | 12 lb/ft' is an interpretation of the W10X12 designation rather than a stated value and is duplicated in both sets; L4X4X5/16 and C3X6 appear on the page but are captured inconsistently across the sets.
